inScope.q: When can I go see the professor?
inScope.evidence: Wednesdays from 10:00 a.m. to noon

inScope.q: Where are the TA's drop-in hours held?
inScope.evidence: in the newsroom on the second floor

inScope.q: How much is the final feature worth?
inScope.evidence: counts for 20 of the 60 story points

inScope.q: How many people do I need to interview for each story?
inScope.evidence: at least two named human sources

inScope.q: Can I use a press release as one of my sources?
inScope.evidence: Press releases, social media posts

inScope.q: What happens if I turn my story in two days late?
inScope.evidence: lose one letter grade for each day

inScope.q: Can I get an extension on the last story?
inScope.evidence: except the final feature

inScope.q: What if I spell someone's name wrong in my story?
inScope.evidence: automatic F on that assignment

inScope.q: Is there any way to get points back after a factual mistake?
inScope.evidence: filing a correction memo within 48 hours

inScope.q: Do you drop the worst style quiz?
inScope.evidence: Your lowest quiz score is dropped

inScope.q: How many classes can I skip without losing points?
inScope.evidence: miss two classes for any reason

inScope.q: Am I allowed to use ChatGPT for my stories?
inScope.evidence: use AI tools to check grammar

inScope.q: Why do news stories put the key facts at the top?
inScope.evidence: most people read only the first few paragraphs

inScope.q: How long should a hard news lede be?
inScope.evidence: about 25 to 35 words

inScope.q: Should I start my lede with the date of the event?
inScope.evidence: Avoid starting a lede with a date

inScope.q: When is it OK to open with an anecdote instead of the news?
inScope.evidence: Use delayed ledes for features

inScope.q: What is a nut graf and where does it go?
inScope.evidence: third to fifth paragraph

inScope.q: Can I fix the grammar inside a direct quote?
inScope.evidence: Never change the words inside quotation marks

inScope.q: Which verb should I use for attribution?
inScope.evidence: "said" is almost always the right verb

inScope.q: How do I refer to a source the second time I mention them?
inScope.evidence: use only the last name

inScope.q: How long is a news brief supposed to be?
inScope.evidence: 150 to 250 words

inScope.q: What is a kicker?
inScope.evidence: a final quote or detail that echoes the lede

inScope.q: What should I ask at the end of an interview?
inScope.evidence: Who else should I talk to?

inScope.q: Can I interview my roommate for a class story?
inScope.evidence: Do not interview friends, family members, or roommates

inScope.q: What's the difference between off the record and on background?
inScope.evidence: the information cannot be published at all

inScope.q: A source told me something and then said it was off the record. Can I still use it?
inScope.evidence: must be made before the source says the information

inScope.q: When is it acceptable to keep a source's name out of the story?
inScope.evidence: the source faces real harm

inScope.q: How can I check whether a viral photo is real?
inScope.evidence: reverse image search

inScope.q: Should numbers under 10 be written out in words?
inScope.evidence: Spell out the numbers one through nine

inScope.q: Does AP style use the Oxford comma?
inScope.evidence: does not use the Oxford comma in a simple series
